title: Hosted API: Region pinset verifier and residency safeguard orchestration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Several enterprise customers require provable data residency for Hosted API traffic and automated retention evidence for audits. Current pin controls allow setting preferred regions but do not produce a verifiable evidence artifact or automated verification reports. This ticket scopes a new component (Pinset Verifier + Safeguard Orchestrator) that: 1) validates tenant pinsets against runtime routing decisions, 2) produces signed evidence bundles for compliance audits (JSON + signed manifest), 3) enforces soft and hard fallback policies when capacity or outages would violate residency, and 4) integrates with the Console and Audit export pipeline. Goals: - Deterministic verification: for every request routed under a tenant pinset, the verifier must log the routing decision and include it in periodic evidence bundles. - Automated evidence packaging: bundles include request hashes, routing path, model variant, timestamp, signed attestations, and TTL/retention metadata. - Safeguard orchestration: when a routing decision would violate a hard residency pin, automatically block or apply pre-approved canary fallback (soft-fail) depending on tenant policy, and generate an exception event with remediation steps. - Operator tooling: Console views for pinset status, recent exceptions, and exportable compliance bundles (S3 or signed download). Out of scope: changes to Dedicated/private deployment behavior (those are tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: Pinset Verifier exists as a service hook that receives routing events and tenant pinset metadata.
Evidence bundles can be generated on-demand and on a configured cadence (daily/weekly) and include signed manifest with key id.
Bundles include: tenant id, request id list (or hashed ids for privacy), region used, model version, timestamp range, and retention TTL metadata.
When a routing decision would violate a tenant's hard pin, the system either blocks the request or applies a tenant-configured soft-fail policy; the decision and justification are recorded.
Console shows a Pinset Compliance dashboard with last verification run, drift score, number of exceptions, and download/export action.
Automated tests cover verifier logic, evidence bundle format, and retention expiration handling.
Legal and Security approve the evidence bundle format and signing approach (HSM-backed key rotation documented).
Operational runbook created for escalations and manual attestation replays.
Performance impact on tail latency is <5ms for the verification hook in steady state (benchmarked).

notes: Implementation approach: lightweight stream consumer -> compact event store (per-tenant shards) -> bundle composer job. Optimize storage by storing request hashes and sampling at 100% for tenants with compliance=true, otherwise adaptive sample.
Trade-offs: Full request capture would simplify audits but increases PII risk and storage costs. We will default to hashed ids + metadata and require tenant opt-in for transcript retention.

Fallback policies: three modes: HARD_BLOCK (reject routing that breaks pin), SOFT_FAIL (route but mark event and notify tenant/ops), LOG_ONLY (no enforcement, only monitoring). Tenants choose per-pinset.
Evidence signing: use customer-sequestered KMS key OR Redwood HSM key depending on tenant contract. Include key-id and certificate chain in manifest. Rotation window: 90 days recommended.
Alerting: create alerts for >0.1% drift rate for high-compliance tenants and for any HARD_BLOCK events with >=5% rejection rate in 1h.
Privacy: avoid including raw prompt/response unless tenant explicitly requests sample inclusion with SLA impact documented.
audit_flow: 1) Routing event emitted -> verifier consumes -> compact record persisted. 2) Daily bundler assembles records for tenant time window -> compress and sign with KMS -> upload to secured S3 bucket with tenant prefix -> register bundle in Compliance Ledger -> notify tenant admin via console and webhook. 3) Bundle retention follows tenant retention policy; deletion job removes bundles and writes tombstone event to ledger for auditability.
operator_runbook: How to trigger on-demand bundle generation via admin Console
Steps to rotate signer key and re-sign existing bundles (if required by contract)
Procedure for responding to HARD_BLOCK spike: identify root cause (capacity vs misconfigured pin) and steps to remediate
